// CONFIG_3014_NOTE: LibreLane 3.0.14 variant of gpu/config.json, generated 2026-09-10. The original config.json is left byte-identical so the existing GPU sign-off stays reproducible -- same discipline as cpu/config_3014.json and soc/config_multiclock.json. GPU-SPECIFIC SETTINGS DELIBERATELY PRESERVED, each the result of a prior failure: SYNTH_STRATEGY 'DELAY 2' (DELAY 3 timed out at 2h48m+ on this 425K-gate design), PL_TIME_DRIVEN false (timing-driven GPL 2nd pass OOM-kills on <=16 GiB hosts), and SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES false (yosys 'share' SAT pass hangs on the 8-lane vector_alu shifters). Do not 'clean these up'.
// LAYERS_RC_NOTE: Converted from the flat '<layer> <cap> <res>' string to 3.0.14's nested per-IPVT-corner mapping. NOTE THE OLD ORDER IS CAP-THEN-RES. M1 ADDED (bead gyx): the ASAP7 tech LEF carries no RESISTANCE/CAPACITANCE on ANY routing layer, and librelane's irdrop.tcl sources set_rc.tcl, so LAYERS_RC is what feeds PSM -- without M1 here, analyze_power_grid reports PSM-0021 zero-resistance. Values are ORFS's own.
// UNITS_S9F_1: librelane declares PL/GRT_RESIZER_*_SLACK_MARGIN as units=ns in its schema, but scripts/openroad/rsz_timing_post{cts,grt}.tcl pass the value RAW to OpenROAD, which reads it in the Liberty time_unit. ASAP7 Liberty is time_unit 1ps -- so these are PS values, NOT ns. The old 0.075/0.100 values meant 0.075-0.1 ps (~0 guard band). See claude_verilog_test-s9f.
// UNITS_S9F_2: Values below are real ps, sized at 2.5% of the 1750 ps GPU/fabric period for setup / 1.5% for hold, rounded to 5 ps -- the same percentage basis used for the CPU (780 ps) and SoC (1750 ps) configs so all three ASAP7 designs share one policy. Re-validate on the next real ASAP7 GPU PD run -- not exercised here.
// PIN_ORDER_NOTE: FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG pins the macro's boundary pin SIDE AND ORDER. Without it OpenROAD free-floats pin assignment per block run -- measured on the CPU macro (GH #96): two consecutive regenerations moved 393 of 401 pins, which perturbed SoC placement around u_cpu and took cpu_clk setup WNS from -60.66 to -596.00 ps (see pnr/asap7/cpu/README_pin_order.md). This file's side/order was generated from the checked-in, run-23-signed-off pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.lef -- it is generated, not hand-tuned, because the GPU has no measured timing problem to tune against. NOTE: pinning side+order does NOT reproduce that LEF's absolute pin coordinates -- io_place distributes pins evenly along each edge, while the checked-in LEF's spacing came from irregular free-floating placement, so the first regeneration under this file will shift the boundary once (measured: median 42.6um / max 223.5um, order-preserving, 0/325 pins land on the old coordinates) before becoming stable forever. See pnr/asap7/gpu/README_pin_order.md for the full measurement and the correct determinism criterion (same cfg -> identical output across runs, not '0 pins moved vs the old LEF'). io_place.py ERRORS if a design pin is missing from the file or vice versa (power/ground are excluded by the tool), so adding a port fails loudly instead of silently reshuffling.
// DRT_OPT_ITERS_NOTE: Bounded to 12 (3.0.14 default is 64). On the CPU block the measured trade-off was 12 iters -> 2045 DRC / 12 GiB peak / 3h25m and COMPLETES, versus 64 -> 43 DRC but 13 GiB peak and DIED before write_views. The GPU is ~11x the CPU's instance count (814,908 vs 75,194), so peak memory is the binding risk on this 15.9 GB host -- start bounded and only raise it if the run completes with headroom.
// SPEF_NOTE: RUN_SPEF_EXTRACTION/RUN_MCSTA enabled for bead e69's GPU half. The real ORFS OpenRCX deck is already installed and CPU-validated; what was missing until 2026-09-09 was a run with actual routed wires to extract from. Validate this block on its own before trusting any extracted number, mirroring the CPU note at pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json:127.
// DRT_THREADS_NOTE: 2 threads (was 12). Thread count IS a memory multiplier (each TritonRoute worker holds its own routing state) and 2 is kept for that reason -- but it is NOT what killed the GPU runs. ROOT CAUSE (2026-09-11, bead e69): all three GPU detailed-routing deaths (2026-09-10 14:31:43, 20:19:54; 2026-09-11 00:44:20) were systemd-oomd PRESSURE kills of the whole terminal scope, at 'Start 0th optimization iteration'. True peak VmHWM was a flat 14.05 GiB with 32 GiB swap free -- capacity was never the wall. oomd monitors user@1000.service at 50% PSI over 20 s. Stop systemd-oomd (sudo) for the duration of GPU/SoC detailed routing, then restart it.
// DIODE_NOTE: ASAP7 SIMPLE HAS NO ANTENNA DIODE. The PDK config sets DIODE_CELL=DECAPx1_ASAP7_75t_R with DIODE_CELL_PIN="" (libs.tech/openlane/asap7sc7p5t_SIMPLE/config.tcl:69-70); DECAPx1 is a decap whose only pins are VDD/VSS. LibreLane 3.0.14 joins the two into 'DECAPx1_ASAP7_75t_R/', and odbpy/diodes.py:248 then does findITerm('') -> None -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'connect'. Killed RUN_2026-09-12_10-27-19 at step 42 (odb-diodesonports). Earlier runs never hit it because they were launched with a narrower step set, not because the config differed. Both flags off: there is no cell to insert, so neither step can ever succeed on this PDK. ALSO: repair_antennas itself fails -- antenna_repair.tcl:27 dies with "can't read 'diode_mterm'" because OpenROAD needs a diode PORT and DECAPx1 has none. That killed RUN_2026-09-12_11-03-29 at step 43 (openroad-repairantennas). So RUN_ANTENNA_REPAIR=false and DRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_ITERS=0 too -- the latter matters most: drt.tcl runs the same repair_antennas AFTER detailed routing, which would throw away hours of work. Antenna repair is simply not available on ASAP7 SIMPLE; antenna CHECKING still runs.
